author: TEDx Talks
description:
A dangerous misunderstanding is pushing the world to race for achieving AGI. In this provacative talk, Alvin examines the underlying motivations of why AI labs globally are behaving so recklessly with such a transformative technology. And more importantly, what the people of the world needs to do to ensure we nudge the future towards the positive outcome we deserve.  Alvin Wang Graylin is a global technology strategist, author of Our Next Reality (Hachette), and Chairman of the Virtual World Society. Over a 35+ year career spanning AI, semiconductors, immersive computing, and cybersecurity, he has held senior leadership roles at HTC, Intel, IBM, and Trend Micro, founded four venture-backed startups, and invested in over 100 early-stage technology companies.

description:
We are constantly told that procrastination is the enemy of productivity, but what if it is actually the secret to creativity? In this perspective-shifting talk, Suzzeet Shrestha reframes the guilt associated with delaying tasks, explaining how the mind uses idle time to synthesize existing ideas into something entirely fresh. She offers a new framework for understanding our work habits, showing how to leverage procrastination as a deliberate and powerful creative process.

Suzzeet Shrestha is a marketing and communications professional currently serving as the Marketing and Communication Manager at F1Soft International. Drawing from her experience in fast-paced corporate environments, she challenges traditional productivity norms and explores how counter-intuitive approaches can drive innovation and authentic self-expression in both life and work.

title: Procrastination as Your Creative Process | Suzzeet Shrestha | TEDxSoftwarica College

description:
What happens when society’s focus on youth causes us to overlook the value of experience?
Leadership and culture strategist Dan Pontefract explores the growing issue of ageism in society and the workplace. Through personal experiences and professional insights, Dan challenges the assumption that innovation and success belong only to younger generations, arguing that organizations risk losing valuable knowledge, wisdom, and perspective when they overlook experienced voices. Dan Pontefract is a leadership and culture strategist, best-selling author, and consultant with more than 20 years of senior executive experience at SAP, TELUS, and Business Objects. Through Pontefract Group, he has advised organizations including Salesforce, Amgen, Virgin Media O2, Nestlé, Canada Post, Autodesk, BMO, Manulife, the Government of Canada, UBC, and the City of Toronto. He is the award-winning author of six books, including The Future of Work Is Grey, Work-Life Bloom, Lead. Care. Win., Open to Think, Th

author: TEDx Talks
description: In an era of endless scrolling, filters, and ever-changing algorithms, how do you know when you're enough? Drawing from her experiences as a digital storyteller, former beauty pageant queen, and eating disorder survivor, Ann Marie Elpa explores how social media has transformed self-improvement into performance. Through personal storytelling, she examines the rise of glow-up culture, the pressures of online validation, and why what many of us are truly searching for isn't perfection, but authentic community. In an era of ever-changing social media algorithms, how do we know we're enough? Digital storyteller and former beauty pageant queen Ann Marie Elpa shares her journey of overcoming an eating disorder while exploring why so many young people struggle with isolation, insecurity, and body image. Based in Toronto, Ann Marie is a social media strategist, freelance journalist, and content creator whose work has appeared in CBC, Business Insider, The Globe and Mail, and The Toronto Star.
title: Chasing the horizon: The glow-up trap and the space in between | Ann Elpa | TEDxTorontoMetU

Happiness expert and keynote speaker Teresa Greco shares a research-backed model to rebuild your inner compass, reconnect with your authentic self, and stay rooted in who you are while living in a technology-driven world. Teresa Greco stands at the intersection of psychology, technology, and well-being. She is a multiple-time TEDx speaker, certified life coach, university lecturer, and PhD student researching inner happiness and human flourishing. She is the founder of Steps to Happiness Coaching, driven by a mission to share the steps that help people live happier, more fulfilling lives. With over 25 years of experience in education as an educator and educational technologies consultant, Teresa brings both research and real-world insight to how we live, learn, and stay human in a digital world. author: TEDx Talks
description:
We often believe growth begins when life becomes clearer, easier, or more certain. Dianna Fioravanti challenges that idea, arguing that possibility begins in the moment we stop waiting for confidence, permission, or perfect timing and choose to move anyway.

Through a deeply personal story of childhood responsibility, hard decisions, and leadership, Dianna explores what it means to “flip the switch” in our own lives. She shows that the stories we believe about ourselves can either keep us small or open the door to who we are becoming. Growth is not something we wait to feel ready for. It is something we decide into.

This talk is a call to anyone standing at the edge of a decision, a dream, or a version of themselves they have not fully stepped into yet: possibility does not always arrive as a perfect plan. Sometimes it begins with one brave decision. Dianna Fioravanti is President at Kuehne+Nagel Canada and the first woman to lead the company in Canada. A transformational leader and
title: You don’t grow into a new life… you decide into it | Dianna Fioravanti | TEDxCambridge University

description:
Em tempos marcados por crises, ansiedade e incertezas, sonhar pode parecer um privilégio. Mas, e se sonhar for justamente o primeiro passo para transformar a realidade?
Nesta palestra, a psicóloga, multiartista e ativista propõe uma reflexão sobre o poder da imaginação como ferramenta de resistência, regeneração e mudança social. Unindo psicologia, neurobiologia, ancestralidade e arte, ela convida o público a resgatar a capacidade de imaginar novos futuros, romper narrativas limitantes e construir, coletivamente, caminhos mais humanos, criativos e igualitários.
Porque, antes de transformar o mundo, precisamos ser capazes de sonhá-lo. Milena Munhoz, psicóloga, multiartista e ativista, atua na psicologia social e comunitária promovendo processos de expressão, consciência e transformação por meio da arte e da psicologia. Guiada pela crença de que sonhar é um ato de coragem e urgência, conecta neurobiologia, ancestralidade e imaginação como caminhos para a regeneração social e a construçã

La esperanza dada en que nos conectamos y apoyamos los unos a los otros. description: A powerful call to treat water conservation as a shared, collective responsibility — exploring how community-driven river revival and water harvesting can restore ecosystems, rebuild rural economies, and bring lasting water security to drought-prone regions. Widely known as the "Waterman of India," Dr. Rajendra Singh is an environmentalist from Alwar district in Rajasthan who has spent decades leading community-based efforts in water harvesting and river revival through his organisation Tarun Bharat Sangh, helping restore water security to hundreds of villages in some of India's most drought-prone regions. For his pioneering work, he received the Ramon Magsaysay Award for Community Leadership in 2001 and the Stockholm Water Prize in 2015, often referred to as the "Nobel Prize for water." description: Dr. Ashu Jain presented her reflection on reinvention and resilience, highlighting how life’s pauses and challenges can become catalysts for growth, renewal, and personal transformation. Ashu Jain is a remarkable example of reinvention and resilience. Once a homemaker, she has transformed herself into a fitness icon, Instagram influencer, and a contestant on MTV Roadies, inspiring countless people at the age of 57. She completed her B.Tech. in Electrical Engineering in 1989, then spent 23 years as a homemaker before returning to education at age 44. She earned an M.Tech. in Nanotechnology from Jamia Millia Islamia, ranking second in her batch, and went on to complete a PhD from the Indian Institute of Technology, Delhi in 2020 at age 53 - notably, at the same time her granddaughter was completing her own B.Tech. at the same institution. description:
Why doesn't Failure translate into action?
We've all been told that failure is the greatest teacher. But if that's true, why do so many of us keep repeating the same mistakes? Through the story of a student caught in the cycle of trying, failing, and starting over, this talk challenges one of our most common beliefs about growth. Blending psychology with personal experiences, it explores why failure alone doesn't create change, why our brains often pull us back into old habits, and how reducing unnecessary decisions can help turn intention into action. Ultimately, it invites the audience to see failure not as an automatic teacher, but as an opportunity that only becomes growth through consistent action.   Avanti Narwade is an International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme student with a keen interest in psychology, human behaviour, and the science of personal growth. description: In a world filled with constant notifications, entertainment, and endless distractions, boredom has become something we avoid at all costs. But what if boredom isn't a problem to solve, but an opportunity to grow? This talk challenges the belief that we always need to stay busy or stimulated to be productive, exploring how moments of boredom create space for creativity, self-reflection, and original thinking. Boredom isn’t a waste of time, in fact it’s where some of our best thinking begins. This talk challenges the idea that we always need to stay busy or entertained, showing how constant stimulation actually limits creativity and self-awareness. When we allow ourselves to be bored, we make room for deeper ideas, curiosity, and more meaningful connections with ourselves. Instead of avoiding boredom, we should start seeing it as a quiet but powerful tool for growth.
